questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

K, F, Y, T, ?, H, A, V, O
questions.solution:
Split the series into alternate terms.
- Odd places (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th): K, Y, ?, A, O
- Even places (2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th): F, T, H, V

In each sub-series every term moves 14 letters forward, cycling back to A after Z: F$\to$T$\to$H$\to$V (positions 6$\to$20$\to$8$\to$22) and K$\to$Y$\to$? $\to$A$\to$O (11$\to$25$\to$13$\to$1$\to$15).

So the missing term is the 13th letter = M.

**Answer: M**
questions.shortcut: Take alternate letters; each jumps 14 places forward (wrapping after Z), so Y + 14 = M.

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the sixth letter cluster in the same way as the first letter cluster is related to the second letter cluster and third letter cluster is related to fourth letter cluster.

EQ : ZK :: CJ : XD :: ? : IR
questions.solution:
From the first cluster to the second, the 1st letter moves $-5$ and the 2nd letter moves $-6$ (wrapping after A): E$-$5$\to$Z, Q$-$6$\to$K; C$-$5$\to$X, J$-$6$\to$D.

For ? : IR, apply the reverse: I $+5 = 9+5 = 14 =$ N and R $+6 = 18+6 = 24 =$ X.

**Answer: NX**
questions.shortcut: Rule: 1st letter -5, 2nd letter -6; apply it in reverse to IR to get NX.

questions.q:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(HA, JC, OH) (QC, SE, XJ)
questions.solution:
Within each set, both letters of a cluster move $+2$ places to give the next cluster, then $+5$ places to give the third: H$\to$J$\to$O, A$\to$C$\to$H; and Q$\to$S$\to$X, C$\to$E$\to$J.

Checking the options, only (EI, GK, LP) fits: E$\to$G$\to$L and I$\to$K$\to$P.

**Answer: (EI, GK, LP)**
questions.shortcut: Look for +2 then +5 shifts in both letters: EI -> GK -> LP.

questions.q:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(QT, LN, GH) (AU, VO, QI)
questions.solution:
In each set, the 1st letter of successive clusters drops by 5 and the 2nd letter drops by 6 (wrapping after A): Q$\to$L$\to$G, T$\to$N$\to$H; and A$\to$V$\to$Q, U$\to$O$\to$I.

(KD, FX, AR) fits: K$\to$F$\to$A (each $-5$) and D$\to$X$\to$R (each $-6$).

**Answer: (KD, FX, AR)**
questions.shortcut: First letter -5 each step, second letter -6 each step: KD -> FX -> AR.

questions.q: If 19 June 2024 is a Saturday, then what day will 25 December 2024 be?
questions.solution:
Days from 19 June 2024 to 25 December 2024:
$11$ (June) $+ 31 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 25 = 189$ days.

$189 \div 7 = 27$ weeks with remainder 0, so 25 December falls on the same weekday as 19 June.

**Answer: Saturday**
questions.shortcut: Count month-wise days = 189; 189 mod 7 = 0, so same weekday as 19 June = Saturday.

questions.q: If the month of January 2019 ended on Wednesday, then which date was the last Wednesday of June 2019?
questions.solution:
January 2019 ends on 31 January = Wednesday. Days from 31 Jan to 30 June $= 28 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 = 150$; $150 \bmod 7 = 3$, so 30 June = Wednesday + 3 = Saturday.

Wednesdays of June are then 6, 13, 20, 27 - the last one is 27 June.

**Answer: 27**
questions.shortcut: 150 days = 3 odd days, so 30 June = Sat; step back 3 days to the last Wednesday = 27 June.

questions.q:
7 girls A, B, C, X, Y, W and Z are sitting around a circular table facing opposite to the centre (not necessarily in the same order). W is second to the left of X. W is the immediate neighbour of B and C. Z is fourth to the left of B. Y is not the immediate neighbour of C. Which of the following statement is correct?

I. X and W are immediate neighbours of B. II. C is to the immediate left of W.
questions.solution:
All girls face outward, so 'left' = anti-clockwise and 'right' = clockwise.

Fix X; W is 2nd to the left (anti-clockwise) of X, and B, C are the two neighbours of W. If C sat on the X side, Z (4th to the left of B) would land on X - impossible. So B sits between X and W, C on the other side, and the remaining seats go to Z, A, Y with Y kept away from C.

Clockwise order: X, Y, Z, A, C, W, B.
- I: B's neighbours are W and X - true.
- II: one seat anti-clockwise (W's left) from W is C - true.

**Answer: Both I and II**
questions.shortcut: Facing out: left = anti-clockwise. Place X-W-B first; Z forces C to W's anti-clockwise side, so B lies between X and W and C is W's immediate left - both statements true.

questions.q: 7 workers P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in same order). R is the immediate neighbour of T and U. S is the immediate neighbour of P and V. V is second to the left of U. T is second to the right of U. Who is sitting third to the left of Q?
questions.solution:
All face the centre, so 'left' = clockwise and 'right' = anti-clockwise.

Place U. V is 2nd to the left of U and T is 2nd to the right of U. R, a neighbour of both T and U, takes the only seat touching both; S sits beside V, and P must then sit beside S (P's seat also touches nothing forbidden), leaving Q between U and V.

Clockwise order: U, Q, V, S, P, T, R.

From Q, 3 seats clockwise (Q's left): V (1st), S (2nd), P (3rd).

**Answer: P**
questions.shortcut: Facing centre: left = clockwise. Arrange U-Q-V-S-P-T-R clockwise; 3rd clockwise from Q is P.

questions.q: 7 boys A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing opposite to the centre (not necessarily in the same order). F is fifth to the right of G. C is fourth to the left of G. B is the immediate neighbour of F and G. D is not the immediate neighbour of C. A is second to the left of B. What is the position of E with respect to F?
questions.solution:
All boys face outward, so 'left' = anti-clockwise and 'right' = clockwise.

Fix G. F is 5th to the right (clockwise) of G and C is 4th to the left (anti-clockwise) of G. B, a neighbour of both F and G, takes the only seat between them. A is 2nd to the left (anti-clockwise) of B; D then cannot sit beside C, which fixes D and E uniquely.

Clockwise order: G, D, E, C, A, F, B.

From F, moving anti-clockwise (F's left): A (1st), C (2nd), E (3rd).

**Answer: Third to the left**
questions.shortcut: Facing out: left = anti-clockwise. Order G-D-E-C-A-F-B clockwise; E is 3 anti-clockwise seats from F.

questions.q: From the following options, choose the one word that cannot be formed using the letters of the word 'EXPLANATION'.
questions.solution:
EXPLANATION = E, X, P, L, A, N, A, T, I, O, N. The letter C does not appear in it, so CAT cannot be formed. PLAN, AXLE and LATE can all be made from the available letters.

**Answer: CAT**
questions.shortcut: Scan for a letter missing from EXPLANATION - there is no C, so CAT is out.

questions.q: In the following among four alternatives, which of the following cannot be formed using the letters of the word 'CONSIDERATION'?
questions.solution:
CONSIDERATION = C, O, N, S, I, D, E, R, A, T, I, O, N - only two N's and no M. DENOMINATION needs three N's and an M, so it cannot be formed. DONATION, RATION and CONSIDER all fit within the available letters.

**Answer: DENOMINATION**
questions.shortcut: DENOMINATION has three N's and an M; CONSIDERATION has only two N's and no M.

questions.q: In a farm, there are cows and hens. The total number of heads is 50 and the total number of legs is 140. How many hens are there?
questions.solution:
Let cows $= c$, hens $= h$.
$c + h = 50$ and $4c + 2h = 140$.

Subtracting twice the first equation: $2c = 140 - 100 = 40 \Rightarrow c = 20$, so $h = 50 - 20 = 30$.

**Answer: 30**
questions.shortcut: Extra legs over 2 per head: 140 - 2(50) = 40 -> cows = 20, so hens = 30.

questions.q:
Identify the wrong number in the following series.

0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 21, 34
questions.solution:
The series follows the Fibonacci rule - each term is the sum of the two before it: $0+1=1$, $1+1=2$, $2+3=5$, $3+5=8$.

The next term should be $5+8 = 13$, not 12. With 13 in place, $8+13=21$ and $13+21=34$ hold, so 12 is the wrong number.

**Answer: 12**
questions.shortcut: Fibonacci: 5 + 8 = 13, so 12 breaks the chain.

questions.q:
Find the next number in the sequence.

5, 13, 44, 183, 926, ?
questions.solution:
Pattern: $\times 2+3$, $\times 3+5$, $\times 4+7$, $\times 5+11$, $\times 6+13$ - multipliers run 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and the added numbers are the primes 3, 5, 7, 11, 13.

$183 \times 5 + 11 = 926$; next $= 926 \times 6 + 13 = 5556 + 13 = 5569$.

**Answer: 5569**
questions.shortcut: Multiply by 2,3,4,5,6 and add primes 3,5,7,11,13: 926 x 6 + 13 = 5569.

questions.q:
Find the next term in the sequence.

2B, 9D, 28G, 65K, 126P, ?
questions.shortcut: n^3 + 1 gives 217; letter gaps +2,+3,+4,+5,+6 -> V.

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the first letter-number cluster in the same way as the fourth letter-number cluster is related to the third letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 - Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

LQT150 : ? :: TVP250 : SYW470 :: UKL350 : ONX570
questions.solution:
Number: 250$\to$470 and 350$\to$570 show a constant $+220$; hence 150$\to$370.

Letters: reverse the cluster and shift every letter $+3$: TVP$\to$PVT$\to$SYW and UKL$\to$LKU$\to$ONX. So LQT$\to$TQL$\to$WTO.

**Answer: WTO370**
questions.shortcut: Number +220; reverse the three letters and add 3 to each (TQL -> WTO).

questions.q:
Arrange the given words in the sequence in which they occur in the dictionary.

1. Since 2. Sink 3. Sing 4. Single 5. Sin
questions.solution:
Alphabetical order: Sin $<$ Since $<$ Sing $<$ Single $<$ Sink. A shorter word comes before its extension (Sin, Sing); among the common stem 'sin...', 'c' $<$ 'g' $<$ 'k' places Since, then Sing/Single, then Sink.

So the order is 5, 1, 3, 4, 2.

**Answer: 51342**
questions.shortcut: Sin < Since < Sing < Single < Sink -> 51342.

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and fourth number is related to third number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 - Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

546 : 511 :: 9745 : 9710 :: 5736 : ?
questions.shortcut: Simply subtract 35: 5736 - 35 = 5701.

questions.q:
In a certain coded language 'PART' is coded as 'QDPO' and 'GUNS' is coded as 'HXLN'.

How will 'BONK' be coded in the same code language?
questions.solution:
Letter shifts from word to code: $+1, +3, -2, -5$ (P$\to$Q, A$\to$D, R$\to$P, T$\to$O; GUNS$\to$HXLN confirms it).

Applying to BONK: B$\to$C, O$\to$R, N$\to$L, K$\to$F $\Rightarrow$ CRLF.

**Answer: CRLF**
questions.shortcut: Shifts +1, +3, -2, -5 on B-O-N-K give CRLF.

questions.q:
In a certain coded language 'BEAMS' is coded as 'CHFLQ' and 'ARISE' is coded as 'BUNRC'.

How will 'CONGO' be coded in the same code language?
questions.solution:
Letter shifts: $+1, +3, +5, -1, -2$ (BEAMS$\to$CHFLQ and ARISE$\to$BUNRC both confirm it).

Applying to CONGO: C$\to$D, O$\to$R, N$\to$S, G$\to$F, O$\to$M $\Rightarrow$ DRSFM.

**Answer: DRSFM**
questions.shortcut: Shifts +1, +3, +5, -1, -2 on C-O-N-G-O give DRSFM.
